### Banner Corporation Reports Net Income of $47.7 Million, or $1.36 Per Diluted Share, for Third Quarter 2026; Declares Quarterly Cash Dividend of $0.52 Per Share; Results Strengthened by Completion of Pacific Financial Corporation Acquisition


10/21/2026


WALLA WALLA, Wash.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Banner Corporation (NASDAQ:BANR) (“Banner”), the parent company of Banner Bank, today reported net income of $47.7 million, or $1.36 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $48.9 million, or $1.43 per diluted share, for the preceding quarter, and $53.5 million, or $1.54 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025. Net interest income was $161.9 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $153.7 million in the preceding quarter and $150.0 million for the third quarter a year ago. The increase in net interest income compared to both the prior quarter and the third quarter a year ago was primarily driven by an increase in average interest-earning assets resulting from the acquisition of Pacific Financial Corporation (“Pacific Financial”) on September 1, 2026 and organic loan growth, as well as expansion in Banner’s net interest margin reflecting higher yields on interest-earning assets. Funding costs increased compared to the prior quarter, partially offsetting the increase in interest income, but decreased compared to the third quarter a year ago. Third quarter 2026 results included $5.2 million of merger-and acquisition-related costs, compared to $238,000 in the preceding quarter and none in the third quarter of 2025. Third quarter 2026 results also included a $2.8 million provision for credit losses, compared to $3.8 million in the preceding quarter and $2.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.


Net income was $151.3 million, or $4.39 per diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income of $144.1 million, or $4.15 per diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 included a $5.8 million provision for credit losses, a $3.3 million net loss on the sale of securities and a $1.8 million net increase in fair value adjustments on financial instruments carried at fair value, compared to a $10.6 million provision for credit losses, a $374,000 net gain on the sale of securities and a $626,000 net increase in the fair value adjustments on financial instruments carried at fair value during the same period in 2025. The nine months ended September 30, 2026 results included $5.4 million of merger and acquisition related costs, compared to none for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.


Banner announced that its Board of Directors declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.52 per share payable November 13, 2026, to common shareholders of record on November 5, 2026.


“During the third quarter, we completed the merger with Pacific Financial Corporation, the holding company of Bank of the Pacific,” said Mark Grescovich, President and CEO. “Bank of the Pacific was a highly respected, financially strong community bank with exceptional core deposits. This transaction expands our presence and density in attractive Western Washington and Western Oregon markets while offering Bank of the Pacific customers broader product offerings and technology tools, increased commercial lending limits and an expanded branch delivery system.”


“Banner’s results for the third quarter reflect the continued strength of our super community bank model, which prioritizes deepening client relationships, maintaining a strong funding base, and delivering exceptional service while upholding a moderate risk profile,” Grescovich continued. “Our earnings for the third quarter of 2026 benefited from loan growth and the completion of the merger with Pacific Financial. These benefits were partially offset by higher non-interest expense, which primarily reflects merger related expenses. Banner continues to build on a foundation of solid credit quality, backed by a well-funded credit loss reserve and a robust capital position that offers both resilience and flexibility for future growth. At the same time, the strategic investments we have made across the organization are delivering tangible results, further positioning Banner for long-term success. We also continue to capitalize on a strong core deposit base, with core deposits representing 90% of total deposits at quarter-end. For more than 136 years, Banner has upheld its core values by consistently doing the right thing for our clients, communities, colleagues, company and shareholders. Our long-standing commitment has enabled us to earn trust, navigate change with confidence and continue building a strong foundation for the future.”


At September 30, 2026, Banner, on a consolidated basis, had $18.08 billion in assets, $12.82 billion in net loans and $15.39 billion in deposits. Banner operates 153 full-service branch offices, including branches located in eight of the top 20 largest western United States Metropolitan Statistical Areas by population.


**Third Quarter 2026 Highlights**


- Net interest margin, on a tax equivalent basis, was 4.14% for the current quarter, compared to 4.13% in the preceding quarter and 3.98% in the third quarter a year ago.
- Revenue was $177.3 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $172.0 million in the preceding quarter and increased 4% from $170.7 million in the third quarter a year ago.
- Net interest income was $161.9 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $153.7 million in the preceding quarter and $150.0 million in the third quarter a year ago.
- Return on average assets was 1.11% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 1.20% in the preceding quarter and 1.30% in the third quarter a year ago.
- Net loans receivable increased 8% to $12.82 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $11.83 billion at June 30, 2026, and increased 11% from $11.54 billion at September 30, 2025.
- Loan originations increased to $1.28 billion for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $1.26 billion in the preceding quarter and increased 61% from $794.5 million in the third quarter a year ago.
- Total deposits were $15.39 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $13.79 billion at June 30, 2026, and $14.02 billion at September 30, 2025.
- Core deposits represented 90% of total deposits at September 30, 2026.
- Non-performing assets were $63.0 million, or 0.35% of total assets, at September 30, 2026, compared to $60.5 million, or 0.36% of total assets, at June 30, 2026, and $45.3 million, or 0.27% of total assets, at September 30, 2025.
- The allowance for credit losses - loans was $171.6 million, or 1.32% of total loans receivable, as of September 30, 2026, compared to $161.8 million, or 1.35% of total loans receivable, as of June 30, 2026, and $159.7 million, or 1.36% of total loans receivable, as of September 30, 2025.
- Dividends paid to shareholders were $0.52 per share in the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
- Common shareholders’ equity per share was $58.56 at September 30, 2026, compared to $58.83 at June 30, 2026, and increased 5% from $55.71 at September 30, 2025.
- Tangible common shareholders’ equity per share* decreased 4% to $45.84 at September 30, 2026, compared to $47.82 at June 30, 2026, and increased 2% from $44.79 at September 30, 2025.
- Repurchased 200,000 shares of Banner common stock during the third quarter of 2026 at an average price of $71.03 per share

**Significant Recent Events**


On September 1, 2026, Banner completed the acquisition of Pacific Financial Corporation the holding company for Bank of the Pacific, in an all-stock transaction. At closing, Bank of the Pacific had 18 branch locations, including 15 in Washington and three in Oregon. Shareholders of Pacific Financial received 0.2633 shares of Banner common stock for each share of Pacific Financial common stock they owned, plus cash in lieu of any fractional shares, for total consideration paid of $186.8 million.


The Pacific Financial transaction was accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting. Accordingly, the assets (including identifiable intangible assets) and the liabilities of Pacific Financial were measured at their respective estimated fair values as of the merger date. The excess of the purchase price over the fair value of the net assets acquired was attributed to goodwill. The fair value on the merger date represents management's best estimates based on available information and facts and circumstances in existence on the merger date. The acquisition method of accounting is subject to adjustment within a measurement period of one year from the acquisition date. The acquisition brought $1.29 billion of assets, including $756.9 million of net loans receivable, and $1.14 billion of deposits to Banner.


**Income Statement Review**


Net interest income was $161.9 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $153.7 million in the preceding quarter and $150.0 million in the third quarter a year ago. Net interest margin, on a tax equivalent basis, increased one basis point to 4.14% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 4.13% in the preceding quarter, and increased 16 basis points from 3.98% in the third quarter a year ago. The net interest margin for the current quarter benefited from a higher average yield on interest-earning assets compared to the preceding quarter, partially offset by higher funding costs. Compared to the third quarter a year ago, the increase in the net interest margin primarily reflected lower funding costs and a higher average yield on interest-earning assets.


Interest income was $214.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $202.7 million in the preceding quarter and $205.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. Average yields on interest-earning assets increased five basis points to 5.46% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 5.41% for the preceding quarter, primarily reflecting a higher proportion of loans within the interest-earning asset mix and an increase in loan yields. Compared to the third quarter a year ago, average yields on interest-earning assets increased by three basis points from 5.43%. Average loan yields increased by three basis points to 6.12% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to 6.09% in the preceding quarter, and decreased from 6.17% in the third quarter a year ago.


Interest expense was $52.7 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $48.9 million in the preceding quarter and $55.9 million in the third quarter a year ago. Total deposit costs increased by five basis points to 1.38% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to 1.33% in the preceding quarter, and decreased by 12 basis points compared to 1.50% in the third quarter a year ago. The increase in deposit costs compared to the preceding quarter was primarily due to higher average rates paid across all deposit categories and a shift in deposit mix toward interest-bearing deposits, partially offset by growth in non-interest-bearing deposits. The decrease in deposit costs in the current quarter compared to the same quarter a year ago primarily reflected lower average rates paid across all deposit categories.


The average rate paid on borrowings increased 11 basis points to 3.99% in the third quarter of 2026 from 3.88% in the preceding quarter, primarily reflecting higher average rates paid on borrowings and lower FHLB advances in the current quarter. The average rate paid on borrowings decreased by 19 basis points from 4.18% in the third quarter a year ago, primarily due to lower average rates paid on FHLB advances and junior subordinated debentures and subordinated notes, partially offset by a higher average rate paid on other borrowings. The total cost of funding liabilities increased four basis points to 1.43% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to 1.39% in the preceding quarter, and decreased 14 basis points from 1.57% in the third quarter a year ago.


A $2.8 million provision for credit losses was recorded in the current quarter (comprised of a $1.8 million provision for credit losses - loans and a $1.0 million provision for credit losses - unfunded loan commitments). This compares to a $3.8 million provision for credit losses in the prior quarter (comprised of a $1.6 million provision for credit losses - loans and a $2.2 million provision for credit losses - unfunded loan commitments) and a $2.7 million provision for credit losses in the third quarter a year ago (comprised of a $1.4 million provision for credit losses - loans and a $1.3 million provision for credit losses - unfunded loan commitments). The provision for credit losses recorded in the third quarter of 2026 primarily reflected loan growth, partially offset by improvements in credit quality.


Total non-interest income was $15.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $18.2 million in the preceding quarter and $20.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease from the preceding quarter was driven primarily by a net loss on the sale of securities of $2.1 million, resulting from the sale of the investment portfolio acquired from Pacific Financial, as well as a $630,000 decrease in miscellaneous income, reflecting lower gains on SBA loan sales and fluctuations in other miscellaneous income items. These decreases were partially offset by a $470,000 favorable change in fair value adjustments on financial instruments. Compared to the prior year quarter, non-interest income decreased primarily due to lower miscellaneous income, as well as lower mortgage banking revenue. These declines were partially offset by higher deposit fees and other service charges. Total non-interest income was $52.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $57.6 million for the same period in 2025.


Total non-interest expense was $115.7 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $108.0 million in the preceding quarter and $102.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. Merger-related expenses were $5.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $238,000 in the preceding quarter and none in the third quarter of 2025. Excluding merger-related expenses, the increase from the preceding quarter reflected increases in expenses in several categories related to the acquired Pacific Financial operations, including an increase in salary and employee benefits. In addition, real estate operations expense increased by $1.1 million, reflecting write-downs of foreclosed real estate. The increase compared to the same quarter a year ago primarily reflects increases in salary and employee benefits, information and computer data services expenses, professional and legal expenses, and real estate operations expenses, partially offset by a decrease in occupancy and equipment expense. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, total non-interest expense was $326.3 million, compared to $304.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.


Banner’s efficiency ratio was 65.25% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 62.80% in the preceding quarter and 59.76% in the same quarter a year ago. Banner’s adjusted efficiency ratio, a non-GAAP financial measure, was 59.53% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 61.30% in the preceding quarter and 58.54% in the year-ago quarter. See, “Additional Financial Information - Non-GAAP Financial Measures” on the final two pages of this press release for a discussion and reconciliation of non-GAAP financial measures.


**Balance Sheet Review**


Total assets increased 9% to $18.08 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $16.59 billion at June 30, 2026, and increased 9% compared to $16.56 billion at September 30, 2025. The increase for both periods was primarily due to the $1.29 billion of assets acquired in the Pacific Financial acquisition. In addition, both periods benefited from organic loan growth. Securities and interest-bearing deposits held at other banks totaled $3.43 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $3.17 billion at June 30, 2026 and $3.47 billion at September 30, 2025. The average effective duration of the securities portfolio was approximately 6.0 years and 6.4 years at September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively.


Total loans receivable increased 8% to $13.00 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $11.99 billion at June 30, 2026, and increased 11% from $11.70 billion at September 30, 2025. The increase in total loans compared to both periods included $765.5 million of portfolio loans acquired from Pacific Financial.


Commercial real estate loans totaled $4.61 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of 11% from $4.14 billion at June 30, 2026, and 15% from $4.00 billion at September 30, 2025. Commercial business loans totaled $2.73 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of 6% compared to $2.58 billion at June 30, 2026, and an increase of 12% from $2.43 billion at September 30, 2025. Growth in both categories reflected the Pacific Financial acquisition and new loan production, partially offset by payoffs and paydowns.


Multifamily real estate loans totaled $913.3 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of 7% from $855.9 million at June 30, 2026, and 6% from $860.7 million at September 30, 2025. Construction, land and land development loans totaled $1.80 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of 6% from $1.69 billion at June 30, 2026, and 4% from $1.74 billion at September 30, 2025. Growth in these categories reflected the acquisition of Pacific Financial, as well as new loan production and advances, partially offset by transfers to the permanent loan portfolios upon completion of the construction phase.


Agricultural business loans totaled $389.2 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of 15% from $337.5 million at June 30, 2026, and 10% from $354.9 million at September 30, 2025, primarily reflecting the acquisition, partially offset by payoffs and paydowns. Consumer loans totaled $929.8 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of 12% from $827.0 million at June 30, 2026, and 26% from $740.3 million at September 30, 2025. The growth primarily reflected the acquisition of Pacific Financial, as well as new loan production and advances, particularly on home equity revolving lines of credit.


Loans held for sale were $32.7 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $27.2 million at June 30, 2026, and $20.3 million at September 30, 2025. One- to four- family residential mortgage held for sale loans sold in the current quarter totaled $103.3 million, compared to $134.6 million in the preceding quarter, and $136.9 million in the third quarter a year ago. The increase in loans held for sale at September 30, 2026, compared to both the preceding quarter and the prior year quarter, was attributable to one- to four-family residential mortgage held for sale loan originations outpacing loan sales during the current quarter.


Total deposits were $15.39 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $13.79 billion at June 30, 2026, and $14.02 billion at September 30, 2025. Core deposits increased to $13.78 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $12.32 billion at June 30, 2026, and $12.48 billion at September 30, 2025. The increase in deposits reflected $1.14 billion in deposits from Pacific Financial during the third quarter of 2026. Excluding acquired deposits, the increase from both the prior quarter and prior year quarter reflected increases in both noninterest-bearing and interest-bearing transaction and savings accounts. Core deposits remained stable at 90% of total deposits at September 30, 2026, and at 89% at both June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025. Certificates of deposit increased 10% to $1.62 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $1.47 billion at June 30, 2026, and increased 5%, compared to $1.54 billion at September 30, 2025, due to the Pacific Financial acquisition.


There were no outstanding FHLB advances at September 30, 2026, compared to $320.0 million outstanding FHLB advances at June 30, 2026, and $100.0 million at September 30, 2025. The decrease in FHLB advances during the quarter reflected repayment of all outstanding advances, as deposits served as the primary source of funding. At September 30, 2026, off-balance sheet liquidity included additional borrowing capacity of $3.82 billion at the FHLB and $1.56 billion at the Federal Reserve, as well as federal funds line of credit agreements with other financial institutions of $125.0 million.


At September 30, 2026, total common shareholders’ equity was $2.13 billion, or 11.80% of total assets, compared to $2.00 billion, or 12.05% of total assets at June 30, 2026, and $1.91 billion, or 11.55% of total assets, at September 30, 2025. The increase in total common shareholders’ equity from June 30, 2026, was primarily due to a $174.6 million increase in common stock, primarily attributable to the acquisition of Pacific Financial during the third quarter. In addition, retained earnings increased by $29.8 million, resulting from $47.7 million in net income, partially offset by the accrual of $17.9 million in cash dividends and a $69.7 million increase in accumulated other comprehensive loss. The Company repurchased 200,000 shares of its common stock in the third quarter of 2026 at an average price of $71.03 per share. At September 30, 2026, tangible common shareholders’ equity, a non-GAAP financial measure, was $1.67 billion, or 9.48% of tangible assets, compared to $1.63 billion, or 10.02% of tangible assets, at June 30, 2026, and $1.54 billion, or 9.50% of tangible assets, at September 30, 2025. See “Additional Financial Information - Non-GAAP Financial Measures” on the final two pages of this press release for a reconciliation of non-GAAP financial measures.


Banner and Banner Bank continue to maintain capital levels in excess of the requirements to be categorized as “well-capitalized.” At September 30, 2026, Banner’s estimated common equity Tier 1 capital ratio was 12.57%, its estimated Tier 1 leverage capital to average assets ratio was 11.59%, and its estimated total capital to risk-weighted assets ratio was 14.42%. These regulatory capital ratios are estimates, pending completion and filing of Banner’s regulatory reports.


**Credit Quality**


The allowance for credit losses - loans was $171.6 million, or 1.32% of total loans receivable and 290% of non-performing loans, at September 30, 2026, compared to $161.8 million, or 1.35% of total loans receivable and 295% of non-performing loans, at June 30, 2026, and $159.7 million, or 1.36% of total loans receivable and 399% of non-performing loans, at September 30, 2025. The allowance ratio decreased compared to both prior periods, primarily reflecting the acquisition of Pacific Financial, which had favorable credit quality and a moderately lower risk profile. Coverage of non-performing loans remained strong at 290% at September 30, 2026, compared to 295% at June 30, 2026. The year-over-year decline from 399% at September 30, 2025 reflects a moderate increase in non-performing loans over the past year, while the allowance level has remained stable and commensurate with the portfolio’s risk profile. In addition to the allowance for credit losses - loans, the allowance for credit losses - unfunded loan commitments was $16.2 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $15.1 million at June 30, 2026, and $14.0 million at September 30, 2025. Net loan charge-offs were $704,000 in the third quarter of 2026, compared to net loan charge-offs of $101,000 and $2.2 million in the preceding quarter and third quarter of 2025, respectively. Non-performing loans were $59.1 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $54.8 million at June 30, 2026, and $40.0 million at September 30, 2025. Despite the increase in non-performing loans, substandard loans declined to $209.7 million at September 30, 2026, from $218.4 million at June 30, 2026. Total non-performing assets were $63.0 million, or 0.35% of total assets, at September 30, 2026, compared to $60.5 million, or 0.36% of total assets, at June 30, 2026, and $45.3 million, or 0.27% of total assets, at September 30, 2025.
